samples.summary: New v1 REST contract changes are documented only in the engine doc, not in the canonical REST doc. `rest-api.md` §5.4 enumerates exactly one merge-related refusal ("A move that would split a merged range returns 409") and says nothing about: the new 409 for a move that would park a block across the freeze; `PUT .../merges` now answering 409 when the map straddles the tab's freeze; `parseMerges` now 400-ing on `MaxMergeEntries` / `MaxMergeCoveredCells`; and — the most caller-visible one — `PUT .../freeze` no longer echoing the requested `{rows, cols}` but returning the snapped boundary it stored. All of that was instead written into `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md` (lines ~128-140), which is the engine's doc, not the API surface's. Per CONTRIBUTING the change should fold into the canonical subsystem doc for the surface it changes; API consumers reading rest-api.md will not learn that an insert/delete or a freeze PUT can silently grow the frozen band.

`docs/design/frontend.md`'s YorkieStore method table still describes `setMerge(anchor, span)` as simply "Write to `root.sheets[tabId].merges[anchorSref]`". After this change it spends a merge budget, can refuse, and returns a boolean the engine must honor — the frontend doc that documents this exact store is not updated, while the sheets doc is. Same doc-drift class as the rest-api gap; cost stays inside the codebase.

The "no merge may straddle the freeze" check is now written out a third and fourth time instead of being shared. `Sheet` has it via `crossesFreezePane` in three call sites, `worksheet-structure.controller.assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` walks a merge map calling `toMergeRange` + `crossesFreezePane`, and `worksheet.controller.assertMergesClearOfFreeze` walks a merge map doing the identical `parseRef`/`toMergeRange`/`crossesFreezePane` loop with a near-identical message. The primitive was shared but the map-walking predicate (e.g. a `findMergeCrossingFreeze(merges, rows, cols)` in `model/worksheet/merging.ts`, beside `snapFreezePastMerges`) was not, so the two controllers can drift in which anchors they consider and what they say about them.

`parseMerges` keeps its own per-span `rs * cs > MaxMergedCells` check even though the change introduces `mergeBudgetAdmits`, which applies exactly that per-span cap as part of the shared predicate. The stated goal of the change ("the ceilings live in the engine... restating them here would let one copy drift") is only half met: the constant is shared but the per-span rule is still restated in the validator, so the API and the engine can diverge in which spans they accept even while reading the same number.

A budget/store refusal of a merge has no user-facing channel, unlike every sibling refusal introduced here. Paste and move refusals go through `RangeOpRefusal` → `setOnRefusal` → `onNotice` with a message in `worksheet.ts`, but `mergeSelection` returning `false` because `store.setMerge` refused (a collaborator grew the map past the budget since this replica loaded), and `applyPasteMerges` silently `continue`-ing on a refused block, produce no notice at all — the toolbar button was enabled, the click does nothing visible, and pasted cells land without their merge. The design doc's own framing ("for an API, silence is indistinguishable from success") argues against leaving the editor silent here.
searchedFor: grep canMergeSelection/mergeSelection call sites in frontend + sheets view

samples.summary: Scope: the change bundles at least five independently user-visible behaviors — (1) merge propagation through copy/cut/paste, (2) the freeze/merge straddle invariant across engine + three API verbs, (3) three new merge-map size ceilings enforced in five writers, (4) a change to clipboard lifetime semantics (paste no longer clears the copy buffer, so repeat pastes stay internal; plus new `revalidateCopyBuffer` axis-ID machinery), and (5) an unrelated `rangeOf` fold rewrite. (4) in particular changes paste behavior for every user regardless of merges, and (3) can now reject writes that previously succeeded. Each is defensible and documented, but reviewing/reverting them as one unit is risky; absent an originating issue scoping all five, this reads as several changes in one.

The doc comment that used to document the removed `MaxMergedCells` constant was converted to a free-floating `/* ... */` block that now sits above `assertInt`, documenting nothing it precedes. Either attach it to the import of the engine constants or move it into the file header.

`MaxMergeEntries`, `MaxMergeCoveredCells` and the `MergeBudget` type are added to the package's public barrel but no consumer outside `packages/sheets` imports them (the backend imports only `MaxMergedCells` and `mergeBudgetError`; the sheets tests import from `src/model/worksheet/merging` directly). Public surface with no consumer is surface the repo has to keep stable for nothing.

CLI doc rows for `sheets.freeze.set` ("an omitted key resets that axis to 0") and `sheets.merges.set` ("replaces the map; omitted anchors are unmerged") no longer describe the full behavior: freeze set may store a boundary past the one requested, and merges set can now be refused (409 straddling freeze, 400 over the map ceilings). The CLI prints the server's response so nothing breaks, but the documented contract is stale.
